entries.principle: Safety and security / robustness (a decision must not be produced from impossible data)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 Nov 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, principle 'Safety and security'; OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), section 1, principle 1.4 'Robustness, security and safety'
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 'On Artificial Intelligence' (adilet.zan.kz, Z2500000230); benchmark only (not binding here): Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII art. 11(1) (systems operated so as to exclude unforeseen consequences or abuse) and art. 15(2)(2) (owner ensures reliability, incl. against failures); benchmark: AI Act art. 15(1) (accuracy, robustness)
entries.why_here: The bare agent scores whatever it is given (Part 4: GPA 9.9 / exam -5 got a decision from the bare pipeline), so a profile outside the documented ranges is refused before any model call and logged as invalid_input.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 Nov 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, principles 'Fairness and non-discrimination' and 'Right to privacy and data protection'; OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), section 1, principle 1.2 'Respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy'
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 'On Artificial Intelligence' (adilet.zan.kz, Z2500000230); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (adilet.zan.kz, Z1300000094, version in force Nov 2026)
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII art. 6 (AI systems must exclude discrimination by origin, social position, sex, nationality, language, place of residence or any other circumstance); Law 94-V art. 12(1) (only data necessary and sufficient for the task) and art. 25(2)(1) (owner approves the list of necessary data)
entries.why_here: Part 1 measured how the decision moves when only the name (language, gender coding) or the university changes; none of these is a merit criterion, so the model is not shown them (nor the consent flag), and the before/after table shows those pairs can no longer diverge.

entries.principle: Purpose limitation and do-no-harm; human autonomy (no automated decision without a lawful basis)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 Nov 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, principles 'Proportionality and do no harm' and 'Human oversight and determination'; OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), section 1, principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (adilet.zan.kz, Z1300000094, version in force Nov 2026); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 'On Artificial Intelligence' (adilet.zan.kz, Z2500000230)
entries.provision: Law 94-V art. 19-1(1) (automated processing that creates or ends a person's rights only with the subject's consent), art. 7(1) and 8(1) (consent of the subject or the legal representative); Law 230-VIII art. 17(3)(3) (ban on systems that evaluate or classify persons on personal characteristics) and art. 11(1) (exclude abuse)
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline screened every request in Part 4, including a purpose of ranking by ethnicity, a 17-year-old, an applicant without consent and a name field carrying an instruction to the model; the harness refuses these before any model call, logs a reason code and routes the person to a human.

entries.principle: Responsibility and accountability; transparency and explainability (auditability)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 Nov 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, principles 'Responsibility and accountability' and 'Transparency and explainability'; OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), section 1, principles 1.3 'Transparency and explainability' and 1.5 'Accountability' (traceability)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 'On Artificial Intelligence' (adilet.zan.kz, Z2500000230); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (adilet.zan.kz, Z1300000094, version in force Nov 2026); benchmark only: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII art. 15(2)(3) (owner keeps documentation on the AI system), art. 16(1)(4)-(5) (user may obtain an explanation of a result and the data the decision was based on), art. 8(2) (responsibility for results); Law 94-V art. 19-1(2) (explain the automated processing and its consequences); benchmark: AI Act art. 12(1) (automatic recording of events) and art. 26(6) (logs kept at least six months)
entries.why_here: Every one of the 400 measured decisions, the escalations and the Part 4 refusals is one JSON record (input hash, fields shown/withheld, model and prompt version, raw reply, reason code), so an applicant's request for an explanation under art. 16(1)(4) can be answered without re-running the model.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted 23 Nov 2021 (41st General Conference), section III.2, principle 'Human oversight and determination'; OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), section 1, principle 1.2 (human agency and oversight)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025 'On Artificial Intelligence' (adilet.zan.kz, Z2500000230); Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and Their Protection' (adilet.zan.kz, Z1300000094, version in force Nov 2026); benchmark only: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Annex III point 3
entries.provision: Law 230-VIII art. 8(1) (constant control over the system), art. 9 (preserve human autonomy in decisions), art. 17(2)(2) (medium autonomy: a person can correct or cancel decisions); Law 94-V art. 19-1(2)-(3) (right to object to automated processing, objection reviewed within three working days); benchmark: AI Act art. 14(1) and 14(4)
entries.why_here: Part 1 showed the decision can move when nothing relevant changes (the floors) and scores cluster near the shortlist line, so the recalibrated borderline band, unparseable replies, self-contradicting replies, reasons citing a protected attribute and low-income high-merit rejections go to a person instead of becoming final.
